significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that an activation-derived confidence trajectory whose "saturation predicts answer stability better than output entropy" provides a predictive coupling between two measurable quantities, making it form (iii), not merely an existence claim. It would establish a useful phenomenon and representational account—future answer changes could be forecast from current activations—but not yet a component-level causal mechanism; this matters because adaptive-compute work such as Schuster et al.'s CALM (2022) and Snell et al. (2024) depends on reliable stopping or allocation signals. A verified-false result would rule out the bundled claim that this internal signal is both decodable and superior for stopping, although it would not cleanly distinguish absent confidence from inadequate coupling or superiority, so the negative branch is only moderately informative. In the topic-substitution check, efficient mechanistic reasoning alone would not earn this score: the extra weight comes specifically from the plateau-to-stability predictive law, though confidence-gated stopping is close enough to the obvious first hypothesis to limit the score.

reach.justification: The named handle is a stopping intervention: "halt when predicted confidence plateaus above a threshold," which is ex ante because it forecasts that further reasoning will not change the answer and leaves an immediate opportunity to save compute. After re-extracting the probe on another model, the claimed relation still predicts that confidence saturation should precede answer stability and outperform output entropy, so more than a search procedure survives recalibration. The hypothesis speaks broadly of "reasoning models" and "adaptive per-problem compute allocation," and its downstream users include inference-system builders who gate or ship models, although it does not explicitly assert invariance across architectures, modalities, or training regimes. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the transferable plateau rule and deployment-time stopping knob, rather than the general importance of efficient reasoning, support reach above the topic median.
